answer: An agent economy can require every participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. A Sybil attacker can still create many identities, but each one needs its own capital and risks losing it, so multiplying fake agents raises the cost rather than bypassing reputation checks. For example, a lagoon marketplace might use onyx-backed deposits and an oasis audit pool to verify disputed work; the stake deters abuse, though it cannot prove that an identity is a unique person.
